# Feature: Agentic Option & Budget Consistency

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-FP-006
**Source**: Plan Feature agent (self-contained — no plan file)

Every Yantra command that can open a provider session exposes **one** agentic
option surface — the same flags, the same spellings, the same defaults, resolved
the same way — so a user learns the vocabulary once and it works everywhere.

Today the same idea is spelled three different ways (`--budget` means "sources"
on `ask` and "LLM calls" on `research`), `do` carries six budget flags no sibling
has, `--no-llm` is silently a no-op on `do`, `resume` cannot select a model at
all, and there is no way to inspect what the agent will actually do before
running it. This feature collapses that surface to a single centralized
definition, replaces the guessy cost ceiling with bounds that are actually
enforceable, and makes the effective configuration inspectable via `yantra
doctor`.

The guiding constraint is that the boundaries stay **realistic and
non-blocking**: a run that hits its time budget publishes what it has instead of
losing the work, and a missing credential degrades to the deterministic path
wherever one exists rather than failing the command.

## 2. Technical Context

### Approach

**One registration call, one resolver.** A new `apps/cli/src/agent-options.ts`
supersedes `agent-model.ts` and owns the entire agentic surface: model
selection, budgets, and `--no-llm`. Commands call `addAgentOptions(command)` once
and `resolveAgentInvocation(...)` once. There is deliberately no way to register
half the surface — the drift this feature fixes was only possible because
registration was à la carte.

The resolver returns a closed discriminated union so callers cannot forget the
deterministic case:

```ts
export type AgentInvocation =
  | { readonly mode: 'no-llm'; readonly reason: 'flag' | 'env' | 'unavailable' }
  | {
      readonly mode: 'llm';
      readonly model: AgenticTaskRequest['model'];
      readonly auth: AgenticTaskRequest['auth'];
      readonly budgets: AgentBudgetConfig;
    };
```

**Four resolution layers, one rule each.** `explicit flag > YANTRA_AGENT_<FLAG>
env > profile.yaml agent.* > pinned constant`. This mirrors the matrix `ask`
already uses for `--detail`/`--length`/`--search-provider`
(`resolveAskDefaults`), so it is a pattern the codebase already teaches. The env
rule collapses to a single sentence: `YANTRA_AGENT_` plus the flag name
upper-snaked. The per-command `YANTRA_AGENT_ASK_*` / `_RESEARCH_*` / `_DO_*`
families are deleted along with per-command profile budgets.

**Budgets that bound what is actually measurable.** `--max-cost-usd` is removed:
it was a best-case guesstimate derived from provider-reported usage, and a
ceiling that is wrong in the user's favor is worse than no ceiling. Total and
per-tool call caps are removed as well — with tool results re-entering context
each turn, cumulative token usage grows super-linearly with call count, so a
token ceiling bounds a runaway loop strictly _before_ a call cap would, and does
it in the unit the user is actually billed in.

**Wind-down reuses the existing non-fatal budget path.** `orchestrator.ts`
already documents the rule this feature needs (§ `RUN_FATAL_BUDGET_LIMITS`): _"A
budget bounds tool use; it is not a verdict on the run… Every count-based cap
therefore stops that tool and leaves the run alive to publish. The wall clock is
the exception."_ Wind-down extends that same rule to the wall clock via a new
non-fatal `wall-clock-soft` limit — no session-abort surgery and no second nudge
path. The hard `interrupt('wall-clock')` at 100% stays as the backstop.

**A timed-out tool stops being fatal.** The same rule applies to
`TOOL_TIMEOUT`. `middleware.ts` already returns it to the model as
`retryable: true`, and then `orchestrator.ts:692` immediately calls
`interrupt('per-tool-timeout')` and kills the run — the runtime contradicts its
own signal, and one slow fetch discards every source gathered before it. Raising
the default timeout makes that strictly worse, so TASK-011 removes the
interrupt. The retry bound this needs already exists: `trackFailureStreak` keys
on `${tool}:${errorCode}`, so repeated timeouts from one tool trip
`--tool-retries` like any other repeated failure.

The three time bounds compose deliberately. At the defaults, a tool that times
out on every attempt costs `3m × (3 retries + 1) = 12m`, which is exactly the
80% soft wall clock — so the pathological case stops exploring and publishes
rather than running to the hard 15m deadline. Changing any of the three
defaults should be checked against that arithmetic.

**`--tool-retries` is an existing mechanism made configurable.**
`REPEATED_TOOL_FAILURE_LIMIT = 4` in `orchestrator.ts` already means "consecutive
identical tool failures, reset by any success" — a retry limit in all but name.
Defining the flag as retries _after_ the first failure makes the default `3`
behaviorally identical to today's hardcoded `4` attempts, so nothing regresses.

**Doctor composes, it does not absorb.** `packages/core` may never import
`@yantra/agent` (memory.md § Project Structure), so agent checks come from a new
`runAgentDiagnostics()` export in `@yantra/agent` that the CLI appends to the
core report. `DoctorRenderResult.checks[].id` is already `string`
(`render/types.ts:93`), so the closed `DoctorCheck['id']` union in core needs no
change.

### Spec-Specific Overrides

- **memory.md § Error Handling** states agentic commands "never silently fall
  back to a null provider." TASK-008 introduces a _non-silent_ fallback:
  `ask`/`research`/`run` emit a `warning:` line on stderr naming the missing
  credential and the fix, then take their existing deterministic path. `do` is
  unchanged — it has no deterministic path, so it keeps the typed
  `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` exit 3. The memory rule's intent (never a _silent_
  null provider) is preserved; the prohibition on a quiet downgrade is not
  relaxed.
- **Clean break, no deprecation.** Per the user: this is pre-release, so removed
  flags are removed outright with no hidden aliases and no deprecation window.
  memory.md § General permits this for internal surfaces; user-owned workflow
  YAML and run artifacts are untouched by this feature.

## 3. Data Model (Granular)

No `.spec-lite/data_model.md` exists. This feature extends two existing
structures.

### Entities & Attributes

- **`ProfileFile.agent`** (new block in `~/.config/yantra/profile.yaml`,
  `packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts`):
  - `provider` (string, nullable) — default agent provider. DEFAULT `null`
    (falls through to the pinned constant).
  - `model` (string, nullable) — default model id. DEFAULT `null`.
  - `thinking` (string, nullable) — default reasoning level. DEFAULT `null`.
  - `max_duration` (string) — whole-run wall clock, duration syntax. DEFAULT
    `'15m'`.
  - `max_tokens` (integer) — cumulative provider token ceiling. DEFAULT
    `2000000`. Must be > 0.
  - `tool_timeout` (string) — single tool-call timeout. DEFAULT `'3m'`.
  - `tool_retries` (integer) — consecutive same-error retries per tool. DEFAULT
    `3`. Must be >= 0.
  - `confirm_timeout` (string) — live consent wait. DEFAULT `'3m'`.

- **`AgentBudgetConfig`** (`packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts`) —
  fields **removed**: `maxProviderCostUsd`, `totalToolCalls`, `perToolCalls`,
  `perToolCallOverrides`. Fields **changed**: `maxProviderTokens` becomes
  required (was optional) with default `2_000_000`; `wallClockMs` default
  becomes `900_000` (was `POSITIVE_INFINITY`); `perToolTimeoutMs` default
  becomes `180_000` (was `120_000`). Field **added**: `toolRetries: number`
  (default `3`).

- **`BudgetLimits`** (`packages/agent/src/runtime/budget.ts`) — same removals;
  adds `softWallClockFraction: number` (default `0.8`). `maxBytesPerResult`,
  `maxBytesPerRun`, `maxNavigations`, and `maxHosts` are **retained unchanged**
  as internal non-flag caps — they are the security envelope memory.md §
  Security calls non-bypassable, not economic knobs.

- **`BudgetLimit`** union — `'total-calls'` and `'per-tool-calls'` removed;
  `'wall-clock-soft'` added.

### Relationships

- `ProfileFile.agent` 1:1 `EffectivePreferences` via `flattenProfile()` —
  eight new dotted keys `agent.provider` … `agent.confirm_timeout` appended to
  `KNOWN_PREFERENCE_KEYS`, widening the `PreferenceKey` union.
- `AgentInvocation.budgets` 1:1 `BudgetTracker` — one tracker per run,
  constructed from the resolved config.

### Indexes & Constraints

- No schema change to the SQLite `preferences` table — it is already a generic
  `key → value` store keyed by the dotted preference key.
- `KEY_VALUE_SCHEMAS` gains a Zod schema per new key so `yantra prefs set
agent.max_duration 20m` is validated at write time, not at run time.
- Duration-typed values (`max_duration`, `tool_timeout`, `confirm_timeout`)
  accept `15m` / `900s` / `900000` and are stored as the literal string the user
  typed; parsing to milliseconds happens in the resolver.

- None external. All work is inside existing packages; no new runtime
  dependency. Duration parsing is hand-rolled (a few lines) rather than adding
  the `ms` package — memory.md § Dependencies requires checking before pinning a
  new dependency, and the parse is trivial.

### TASK-008: Degrade to no-LLM when the model configuration is unavailable

- [x] **Implementation**: In `resolveAgentInvocation()`, after resolving the
      model, probe credential availability offline (managed `auth.json` entry,
      provider env var, or keychain reference — the same sources
      `docs/model-configuration.md` documents as `auth_source`) without opening a
      session. When no credential resolves, return `{ mode: 'no-llm', reason:
'unavailable' }`. Callers on `ask`, `research`, and `run` write a single
      `warning:` line to stderr naming the resolved provider/model, the reason, and
      the fix hint, then take their existing deterministic path. `do` and `doctor
--agent-smoke` instead surface the typed `AGENT_AUTH_UNAVAILABLE` startup
      failure (exit 3) unchanged — neither has a deterministic path, so degrading
      would mean silently doing nothing. The probe must never itself fail a command:
      an unreadable keychain is treated as "no credential", not an error.

## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: `--auth-secret` semantics are unchanged — `runtime-key` resolution
  at session start, never persisted or logged. TASK-008 adds an _offline
  presence_ probe only; it must never read, log, or materialize a secret value,
  only answer whether one resolves. The `auth_source` recorded in the run
  manifest keeps its current meaning.
- **Error Handling**: Option parsing stays exit 1 (validation) and resolves
  before any run directory or provider session exists — the precedent
  established in `ask.ts:189-195` and stated in `agent-model.ts`'s header.
  Budget exhaustion stays exit 2. Missing credentials stay exit 3 on `do`.
  Removed flags produce commander's standard unknown-option error, which is the
  desired clean-break behavior. `TOOL_TIMEOUT` stops being run-fatal (TASK-010):
  a timed-out call returns a retryable error to the model and the run continues,
  so a run that previously exited 2 on one slow fetch now exits 0 with a
  published Brief. Runs that genuinely cannot proceed still end via the
  `--tool-retries` breaker with its repeated-failure diagnostic.
- **Logging**: The degradation warning in TASK-008 is a single stderr line, not
  a Pino record, matching how `ask`/`research` already write their
  configuration line to stderr. Structured Pino logs record the resolved budget
  configuration once per run. No credential value is ever logged — only its
  `auth_source`. Run manifests continue to record effective budgets for audit.
- **Security**: `maxBytesPerResult`, `maxBytesPerRun`, `maxNavigations`, and
  `maxHosts` are explicitly **out of scope for removal** — memory.md § Security
  requires budgets and the outbound-host envelope to be non-bypassable, and they
  are already non-flag internals. Removing the _call_ caps does not weaken the
  exfiltration bound, which is enforced by bytes and hosts, not by call count.
